title: REFINEMENT SYNTHESIS (frontier): failure-mode, anti-evasion and adjudication requirements from items 4-7 plus the steelman
description: The second half of the brief's gate: 'items 4-7 refine it' (docs/civilizational-roadmap-brief.md:57). Consume research items 4 (distinguishing and anti-evasion), 5 (jurisprudencia constante), 6 (administrative and mercantile precedent) and 7 (failure modes), plus item 8 (the mandated Graeber-Wengrow steelman), and produce docs/precedent-research/synthesis-refinements.md - the requirements that T-345 writes into PRECEDENT.md's failure-mode, anti-evasion, adjudication and standing-caution sections. Deliberately has NO build dependency: it consumes research only, so the research half of the epic never waits on the build half. Frontier tier per P-030 (join synthesis is low-verifiability judgment).
acceptance_criteria: OWNS EXACTLY ONE FILE: docs/precedent-research/synthesis-refinements.md. Thinker role - no source edits, and specifically do NOT edit PRECEDENT.md (that is T-345, a worker task that depends on this file). This separation is what keeps the research side free of build dependencies.

CONSOLIDATE the detection signals from item 4 (anti-evasion) and item 7 (failure modes) into ONE numbered, registry-computable list. Each signal: the record fields it consumes, the formula or threshold, the false-positive risk, and a verdict of either 'v0 conflicts pass can compute this' or 'DEFERRED, and here is why and what it would take'. T-345 documents this list; a future follow-on may implement the deferred ones.

DECIDE the repeated-confirmation question from item 5: does a rule bind only after N consistent applications, or on a single verdicted decision? Give the N (or defend N=1), and state whether the answer CHANGES D4 tier 3, adds a tier, or becomes a separate settled flag on the record. Cite the research. If it changes D4, that is an overruling of a coordinator decision and must be recorded as such for the epic join to present to the operator.

EXTRACT from item 6 the non-judicial consistency mechanisms that a CLI plus a JSON registry can actually run in this harness (the register, the standing instruction, the published ordinance, the peer jury) and drop the ones that cannot be mechanised, naming what they would need instead (a human, or an adjudicator agent).

CARRY THE STEELMAN (item 8) into a standing-caution section: the strongest case against the layer, its concrete design consequence, and the falsifiable signals that would decide it. Those signals are the input to the standing quarterly monitoring task T-349 - name them in a form that task can actually track.

SPECIFY the adjudication requirement concretely: precedent disputes must not be settled by a single arbiter (roadmap Part V principle 1, and the scout's observation that coordinator-as-sole-arbiter is exactly the pattern the principle forbids - .harness/context-brief-precedent-layer.md section 3 row 6). State how verifier rotation F6 (ORCHESTRATION.md:119-126) is applied to a precedent conflict, and what the record of an adjudication must contain.
EVERY requirement cites the research document and section that produced it. Requirements with no research basis are labelled as planner judgment.

MUST state, for each requirement, whether it EXTENDS an existing record or would DUPLICATE verification already performed elsewhere (the non-duplication contract from T-339 applies here too - papers/agentic_harness_engineering.pdf:8 Table 3 RQ3a, p.9 non-additive interaction).
Hand off to role verifier. Verification tier: doc/contract tier - internal consistency, citation coverage, and whether each signal is genuinely computable from the fields the schema actually has.

notes.note: plan: consume 04-08 research docs plus coordinator memo and corpus grounding; write docs/precedent-research/synthesis-refinements.md with (1) one consolidated numbered signal list merging item-4 anti-evasion signals and item-7 failure-mode detectors, each with fields/formula/FP-risk/v0-or-DEFERRED verdict, (2) the repeated-confirmation decision vs D4 tier 3, (3) item-6 mechanisable vs non-mechanisable mechanisms, (4) F6-based adjudication spec, (5) steelman standing-caution with T-349-trackable signals, (6) extends-vs-duplicates call per requirement. No source edits.

HANDOFF -> verifier: Replayable evidence: docs/precedent-research/synthesis-refinements.md, sole file written by this task (verify: git status shows only this new file from T-344; no source edits, no PRECEDENT.md edit). All nine acceptance criteria addressed: one consolidated numbered signal list S-01..S-15 merging item 4 (04 section 6) and item 7 (07 sections 1.4/2.3/3.3/4.3), each with fields, formula, false-positive risk, and a v0-or-DEFERRED verdict computed against an explicit field floor stated in section 0 (T-339 still open, contingency disclosed); the repeated-confirmation decision in section 2; item-6 mechanisable/dropped split in section 3; F6-based adjudication spec in section 4; steelman standing-caution with four T-349-trackable signals in section 5; per-requirement EXTENDS/DUPLICATES calls throughout; D1-D8 reconciliation table in section 6. Suggested replay in the document's own section 7. The three hardest design calls, for adversarial attention:

DECISION: N=1 stands - a rule binds on a single verdicted decision; D4 tier 3 UNCHANGED, no coordinator decision overruled. Repeated confirmation is demoted to a non-binding reiterated flag on tier-4 notes (N=3 consecutive non-contrary applications, counter ZEROED by any contrary application, implementation deferred past v0). Grounds: 05 sections 5-8 - both jurisdictions that ran numeric repetition moved toward gated single decisions, and at this harness's citation velocity any N greater than 1 is a de facto ban on binding anything. N=3 itself is disclosed judgment (05 tags it SPECULATION), not doctrine.

TRADEOFF: the forum-shopping citation-completeness check (S-09) ships as mandatory-but-non-blocking inside precedent.py publish - warn plus logged citation_gap event, never a refusal. This takes the doctrinally load-bearing property from 07 section 3.4 (the actor cannot decline to run the check) while refusing the property D6 feared (blocking on false positives trains registry evasion). It EXTENDS D6 rather than overruling it, but the residual argument for a true hard gate at tier-3 publication is real and is recorded for T-348 to put before the operator.

DECISION: adjudication is F6 rotation generalized to precedent conflicts, not a new standing adjudicator role - claiming identity must have produced and verdicted neither conflicting record, escalation keyed to the higher tier, tier-4-vs-tier-4 deliberately not adjudicated (Rule 10 selectivity per 07 section 2.2). Merge is allowed as an ordinary-publication outcome in v0, but a first-class merge verb is a registry-contract change deferred to the T-348 operator gate (08 section 8.2). The domain-qualified-juror strengthening from 06 is left as a named open question, not decided here.

Verification tier: doc/contract per P-024. Key checks: citation coverage on 04 section 6, 05 sections 5-8, 07 section 3.4; and whether each v0 verdict is genuinely computable from the section-0 field floor (re-check against T-339's schema if it has landed).

plan: full P-024 replay - read synthesis-refinements.md and all cited research inputs (04,05,06,07,08 plus coordinator memo, context brief, corpus grounding); trace every requirement to a cited section or D1-D8; check D1/D3/D4/D5/D6 honored, reliability asymmetry encoded, non-duplication contract explicit; verdict done or REJECTED.

DECISION: VERIFIED done. Full P-024 control-plane replay of docs/precedent-research/synthesis-refinements.md against every cited input, read in full: 04-distinguishing-anti-evasion.md, 05-jurisprudencia-constante.md, 06-administrative-mercantile-precedent.md, 07-failure-modes.md, 08-graeber-wengrow-steelman.md, plus .harness/coordinator-decisions-precedent-layer.md (D1-D8), .harness/corpus-grounding-precedent-layer.md, .harness/context-brief-precedent-layer.md section 3, ORCHESTRATION.md:119-126 (F6), and .harness/tasks/T-349.json.

FILE OWNERSHIP (criterion 1): PASS. Sole artifact mtime 05:27:31Z, inside T-344's window (plan note 05:18:45Z, handoff 05:28:10Z). Tracked-file diff is only blackboard.json (CLI-sanctioned), plan.md (mtime 04:35Z = planner task-creation), state.json (mtime 05:15Z, diff is exclusively tasks_done/tasks_failed/last_outcome_at reputation counters auto-written by blackboard.py, pre-dating this task's first note). PRECEDENT.md does not exist on disk, so it was not edited. No source edits. No emojis (non-ASCII limited to section-sign, em dash, right arrow).

CITATION TRACEABILITY (criteria 2, 7): PASS, no fabricated rigor found. Every requirement R-1..R-16 and every signal S-01..S-15 traces to a specific cited section or a coordinator decision, spot-verified section by section: all eight of 04 section 6's signals map onto S-05/S-06/S-07/S-04/S-14/S-01/S-11/S-15 with thresholds and false-positive grades reproduced faithfully (0.7 with n>=3 HIGH; N>=4 MEDIUM-HIGH; difflib MEDIUM; 0.6 with total>=3 LOW-MEDIUM; null-check NONE; 0.4 with >=5; HIGH). 04 section 3's Rodriguez de Quijas quote and the Broome v Cassell norm verified verbatim behind S-03/R-10; 04 frictions 1/2/3 verified behind the D1 refinement, S-07's rationale and S-05's downgrade. 05 sections 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8 and Implications 2/3/4/5 verified behind R-1/R-2/R-3/R-8/R-9, including the SPECULATION tag on N=3 and the D1-grounds rejection of a new tier. 06 sections 1, 2, 3, 4a, 4c, 5, 7, 9, 10 and Implications 1-12 verified behind R-4.1-5, R-5.1-6, R-6, R-7 and the D5 row. 07 sections 1.1-1.4, 2.2-2.3, 3.2-3.4, 4.1-4.3, 5 and Implications 1-8 verified behind S-08/S-09/S-10/S-12/S-13, the engine-shopping non-signal, R-9's escalation ladder and R-11. 08 sections 1.2, 2, 4, 5, 6.1, 6.2, 7.1-7.4, 8.1-8.3 verified behind R-12/R-13/R-14/R-15/R-16. C-1 traces to corpus-grounding section 2's verbatim figures (33.7 precision / 51.4 recall, about 5x random, versus 11.8 / 11.1 against 5.6 / 5.4 baselines, about 2x) and to that report's own design conclusion. C-2 traces to agentic_harness_engineering.pdf:8 Table 3 RQ3a and p.9. R-8's scout citation matches context-brief section 3 row 6 verbatim. R-15's composition claim is confirmed live: T-349 criterion 6 is exactly the two-consecutive-THINNER escalation with a single quarter non-escalating, criterion 3 is the structural-field count, criterion 8 says it consumes T-344's consolidated signals. Planner judgment is labelled where it occurs (R-11 composition, R-14c sequencing, R-16 scope).

COORDINATOR DECISIONS (criteria 3, 6): PASS, none overruled, and the section 6 table's claim to that effect is accurate on independent reading. D1 explicit publication is preserved and reinforced, not weakened: R-2 rejects an auto-binding tier on D1 grounds specifically, and R-4.3 supplies 5 U.S.C. 552(a)(2) as the closest external statutory analogue. D3's PR-NNN is the citable unit in every signal. D4 keeps four tiers each keyed to its observable fact; tier 3 N=1 is confirmed against the item-5 evidence rather than changed, no tier is added, and tier 4 gains only a deferred non-binding flag plus a documentation-only reinterpretation. D5 placement consumed as-is. D6 survives as a pass: the registry-wide sweep is untouched, S-09 never refuses a publication (warn plus a logged citation_gap outcome), engine parity holds because publish is a CLI verb every engine calls, and the residual doctrine-backed argument for a real tier-3 gate from 07 section 3.4 is escalated to T-348 rather than adopted or buried. D7 and D8 honored.

RELIABILITY ASYMMETRY: PASS, encoded on both sides. Ratio is treated as the roughly trustworthy self-declaration, and R-4.4 accepts author-declaration at write time for it explicitly on C-1 grounds. Scope claims are not binding on their author's word: scope_conditions is the baseline against which later records are checked and never a closed statement of reach (section 6 D1 row, sourced to 04 friction 1); C-1 routes every scope-consuming signal (S-06, S-08, S-09) to adversarial confirmation and forbids an auto-verdict; a lower-tier distinguish binds no one but its author (S-02); the semantic half of every scope signal is verifier or adjudicator judgment, permanently and by design (S-03, S-06, S-07, R-6); and R-11.2 requires the adjudicator to restate the scope overlap independently rather than trust either party.

NON-DUPLICATION (criterion 8): PASS and explicit. C-2 states the floor globally and all 15 signals plus all 16 requirements carry an EXTENDS or DUPLICATES call (34 occurrences). No new log file, no new ledger, no parallel verification pipeline and no new locking mechanism is proposed anywhere; the only new-data asks are new event kinds through the existing log_event() call and new fields on the registry record. Verified mechanically that citation_gap and precedent_cited are genuinely absent from the live 31 event kinds (2207 lines), so those are correctly specified as new kinds on the existing log rather than a second substrate. Verifier effort is not duplicated: S-09 sends the verifier to logged citation_gap events instead of a blind re-run, and R-11 confines the adjudicator to the conflict rather than re-verifying the parents' tasks.

COMPUTABILITY (criterion 9): PASS against the stated field floor. All v0 verdicts (S-01, S-02, S-03 structural, S-04, S-05, S-06, S-08, S-13) and both partials (S-07, S-12 citation half) consume only floor fields plus events.jsonl and task notes. All deferrals name a specific missing datum, each confirmed genuinely absent today: no verdict-outcome code on rejection events (S-10, S-11), no fork or lineage identity over the flat blackboard (S-14), no precedent citation event kinds (S-15), free-text revisit_trigger (S-12 trigger half). T-339 is still open, so the section 0 contingency is live and was disclosed rather than assumed away; it was checked, not skipped.

OPEN-QUESTION: four minor items recorded for T-345 and T-342, none blocking. (1) The section 0 field floor omits revisit_trigger even though S-12 and R-14a require it on every binding-tier record; no verdict depends on it, but the field list handed to T-339/T-340 should carry it. (2) S-09's formula embeds one semantically non-computable sub-step, whether a matching record's ratio cuts against the new record's outcome; it reproduces 07 section 3.2 variant 1's own wording and the class-B plus C-1 routing covers the softness, but the shippable half is the mechanical one (a same-scope tier 1-3 record absent from cites) and T-342 should be told which half is the code. (3) S-08's threshold reads two or more records at tier 3 or higher, leaving a tier-3-versus-tier-4 pair unstated; D4 already answers it since tier 4 never binds, and one line would close it. (4) R-1 extends 05 section 6's zero-binding-precedent arithmetic from N=5 to N=2, which 05 supports by implication ("few decisions get cited even twice") but does not state in that form.
